words.gloss: to those who have renounced also
to those who have died also
he who lives in the home

literal: To those who have renounced also, to the destitute also, to those who have died also, he who lives in the home, he who is called, [is] support.
translation: The householder is the true support for those who have renounced the world, for the destitute, and for those who have passed away.
modern: துறவிகளுக்கும், வறுமையால் வாடுபவர்களுக்கும், இறந்துபோனவர்களுக்கும் இல்லறத்தில் வாழ்பவனே துணையாக இருக்கிறான்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the central role of the householder in sustaining society. The word 'இல்வாழ்வான்' refers to the person leading a domestic life, who acts as the foundation for others. He provides 'துணை' (support) to three specific groups who cannot support themselves: 'துறந்தார்' (ascetics who have given up worldly pursuits), 'துவ்வாதவர்' (the destitute who lack basic needs), and 'இறந்தார்' (the departed, who rely on the living for memorial rites). By sustaining these dependent groups, domestic life is shown to be a life of vital service.
